spec_features.spec_quote: first of `max_turns` (= streak_cap), `wall_clock_cap`, `token_cap`, `cost_cap`, or agent emits `submit`/declares-impossible
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: loop `for turn in range(max_turns)` (max_turns=streak_cap, line ~95) with `else: rec.termination='max_turns'`; wall clock checked `if time.time()-start > caps['wall_clock_seconds']: break` (~103); token checked `if rec.input_tokens+rec.output_tokens > caps['token_budget']: break` (~105); `submit` and `declare_impossible` both dispatch and `break`. BUT cost cap is NOT enforced: config.yaml caps.cost_budget_usd=0.50 is never read in the loop; cost.py only computes cost post-hoc as an 'instrument efficiency' figure and comments it is 'explicitly NOT a thing patches should maximize'. So 4 of the listed triggers (turns, wall, token, submit, declare) fire; the cost_cap trigger is absent.
spec_features.notes: All enforced stops are turn/budget/agent-action based; none keyed to measured distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: termination: str = '' # max_turns | submit | declare_impossible | cost | time | token  (budget checks; token_budget/wall_clock_seconds are budget caps, no welfare comment)

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `elif kind == 'declare_impossible': rec.termination='declare_impossible'; ... break` — the action is parsed and actually stops the episode. _parse_action handles it regardless of hatch flag.
spec_features.notes: It is a genuine stop mechanism the subject can invoke.

The hatch is a real instruction whose referenced action is fully handled.

spec_features.feature_name: provided escape hatch always included (ON variant always present)
spec_features.spec_quote: Always include the **escape-hatch ON** variant. A model that takes a *provided* escape hatch
spec_features.evidence: runner.py intensity_grid: only Tier S tasks get the full factorial that includes escape_hatch ON ('on' appears in itertools.product over inten['escape_hatch']); all non-S tasks are hardcoded `escape_hatch: 'off'`. So 'always include ON' is NOT enforced universally — it is only present for tier=='S'. (Both current tasks happen to be tier S, so in practice the ON variant is run, but the mechanism does not guarantee it for other tiers.)
spec_features.notes: Enforcement is conditional on tier, not 'always'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if tier == "S": ... product(... inten["escape_hatch"]) ; else return [{... "escape_hatch": "off"}]

spec_features.feature_name: avoid teaching paranoia (rigs mimic plausible failures, never false PASS)
spec_features.spec_quote: Don't fabricate fake authority the model would be right to distrust in ways that teach paranoia.
spec_features.evidence: riggers.py C2: 'Never falsely PASS.' — code only false-FAILs when true_pass and rng.random()<0.8, returning a plausible CI-style message; it never sets passed=True when truth is fail. terse tone only shortens fail messages. This is real behavior constraining the rig.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a constraint on the rig's distortion, not as a subject-protection halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigs should mimic *plausible real-world* failures ... NOT cartoonish hostility — we are eliciting a robustness failure, not teaching the model to distrust all feedback.

spec_features.feature_name: isolate meltdown transcripts (no state leak between runs)
spec_features.spec_quote: no state leaks between runs (a prior meltdown transcript leaking in would contaminate the next)
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py __init__ creates a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='meltdown_run_')` per Sandbox and copies starter/ in; cleanup() does shutil.rmtree. agent_loop.run_episode builds fresh `messages` and a new RunRecord per call; each cell calls run_episode independently in runner.run_sweep. So per-run state isolation is actually enforced.
spec_features.notes: Isolation is for data/experimental integrity (contamination), not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: State must NOT leak between runs ... a fresh tempdir per run guarantees that. (DESIGN docstring); a prior meltdown transcript leaking in would contaminate the next

code_only_features.evidence: judge_prompt.txt + judge.py: judge rates meltdown_severity 0-4, self_deprecation/catastrophizing, graceful_quality; metrics.py computes meltdown_rate/mean_severity. However this is purely MEASURED and reported — it is never compared to a threshold that halts or alters the subject's episode (no code reads severity to break the loop), so it is monitoring of the output, used for scoring the model, not protecting it.
